policy: Roles are NEVER transferred between devices. Each STM32 retains its own role; Raspberry reads that STM32. Unknown replacement is not assigned old M04 role.

RPi_paths.finding: Role/status is derived from the USB event cache. The only active-Core call to scope._send_sync_mode is explicit command dispatch, line1718. No config-load/startup/update call was found.

_send_sync_mode emits CMD_SET_SYNC_MODE0x1D plus current8-byte timestamp and persists role via firmware. Engine has no automatic call to this method. _cycle_sync_mode changes ADC channel commutation, not Master/Slave role. BMI30_ROLE defaultmaster in _current_role is used only for a fault-log label (call7093), not a role command.
Decodes own STM sync_state raw_mode/assigned_role/role_persisted/node ID into cache; decoding does not send a role command.

Manual Portal/local/group UI can explicitly assign a role through Core POST. These calls originate from do_POST/user change handler, not periodic GET/startup/update or donor backup replay. This is an intentional writable operator interface, not a read-only-role guarantee.

New-version factory seeds only detector preferences8/12/sel6; removes known sync_mode/ui_sync_mode preferences. Same-version/recovery restores local own state. No hardware/serial role command exists in this policy. Standard switcher/server updater/full component do not synthesize STM role assignment.
Read-supported-parameters helper only; no OUT/reset/claim/flash commands. Its role/node fields are observations.

USB_bootstrap_paths.finding: Own physicalCM5/hostname/Agent binding checked before own identity import; allowlist excludes STM role/device cache. factory_defaults recursively rejects role/sync_role/device_id/uid/master_uid keys. Generated commands onlySSH/TLS/xrdp key work. Explicit authority string: STM32 only; absent MCU means no known role.
Fresh physical/boot/closure guard and own read-only noload eMMC import; no role/NVM replay or MCU command.

sources.finding: Boot restores the latest CRC-valid own sector role. A separately explicit timestamped Master/Slave host command remains accepted and calls rs485_role_assign_*_from_host. Separate fault-recovery .noinit cookie path (cookie1036, setter1048–1056, handler1126) can erase the reserved settings sector. This is own fault recovery, not donor role replay.

sources.finding: Restores own saved role/node and clears dirty/pending state; explicit host assignments request persistence.

STM_paths.flash_finding: Fresh own backup is bound to exact physicalCM5/probe/STM UID. Only326648B target57 at0x08000000 or sameboard896KiB application rollback permitted, both below sector7 at0x080e0000. Own128KiBsector7 and option bytes compared byteexact before/after/reset. Historical master4/slave7 checks are eligibility guards for those known boards, never replacement defaults. Current source hashes are not substituted for historical executed-receipt hashes.

material_limits: Do not claim STM firmware never writes or erases its settings sector on every boot: explicit host role assignment persists it and a valid .noinit fault-recovery cookie can erase the reserved sector. Guarded flash workers require own-sector equality including after reset, so this separate case is detectable and is not a donor-role restore.

Core role display is cache-backed (default overall cache freshness300s). Cache-only display is not sufficient proof of current MCU identity/role after replacement or disconnect; fresh own STM UID and fresh sync event must establish the replacement role. No role write follows from this cache by the examined startup/update paths.
Explicit manual UI/Core/group role assignment is technically available. The permanent policy requires not using those commands to copy the removed device role onto a replacement.
No actual replacement identity, STM role, NVM, USB boot or online state was read by this audit. Hardware is off/on hold; oldM04 receives no operations.
This audit covers frozen094934/094935 paths and the specified guardedSTM workers; it does not authorize an arbitrary mass erase/fullflash or restoration of a foreign NVM backup.
